title: Save and load Pocket safely
prompt:
Pocket's storage helpers lose data. Fix them, using the real `localStorage` (in this playground it works but starts empty on every run):

- Fix `saveExpenses(expenses)` so it stores the expenses as JSON under `STORAGE_KEY`.
- Fix `loadExpenses()` so it returns the saved array, and returns an empty array `[]` instead of crashing when nothing is saved, when the saved text is not valid JSON, or when it is valid JSON but not an array.
hints: Log what the starter stores: `[object Object]`. Wrap the data in `JSON.stringify(...)` before `setItem`.
`getItem` returns `null` when nothing was saved. Check for that before parsing.
Put the parse inside `try { … } catch { return []; }`, and finish with `return Array.isArray(data) ? data : [];`.
explanation: `localStorage` only keeps strings, so the array has to be serialised with `JSON.stringify` on the way in; otherwise it is converted with `String()` and becomes `[object Object]`. Loading guards against three different failures: a missing key (`getItem` returns `null`), text that is not JSON (`JSON.parse` throws, which the `catch` turns into an empty list), and JSON of the wrong shape (`Array.isArray` rejects it). The same `try` also catches browsers that block storage entirely, so a page load can never crash here.

checks.saves-json: `saveExpenses` stores the expenses as JSON text
checks.corrupt: Loading invalid JSON returns [] instead of throwing
checks.wrong-shape: Loading JSON that is not an array returns []
